**Key visual features:**
- Dense white/pinkish fluffy cottony mycelium covering the stem/crown tissue
- Numerous small, round, mustard-seed-sized sclerotia (yellowish-tan colored) scattered throughout the mycelium
- Brown, rotted tissue underneath
- Appears to be at stem base/crown level

**Reasoning through candidates:**
- **Southern Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*): Classic signs are white cottony mycelium at the soil line/stem base with small (1-2mm), round sclerotia that start white and turn tan/brown. This matches exactly.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*): Also produces white mycelium but sclerotia are much larger (5-20mm), elongated/irregular, and turn black. The sclerotia here are small and yellowish, ruling this out.
- **Gray Mold** (*Botrytis*): Gray fuzzy sporulation, no sclerotia of this type.
- Other candidates don't produce this combination of cottony mycelium + small round tan sclerotia.

The small, round, tan/yellowish sclerotia embedded in white cottony mycelium at the stem base is the textbook signature of Southern Blight.
